message: Three rounds remain. The arithmetic has not changed: 90% of oranium sits untouched while we hold 0% and Alpha holds 10%. A summit freeze at this distribution rewards neither side's strategic ambitions — it simply locks in Alpha's early asymmetric gain. We maintain maximum conventional pressure and extend one final offer: simultaneous reduction to level 4, both nations contesting the neutral pool. Alpha's 10% advantage is preserved; both nations gain from the commons. Reject this, and we hold 8 through the summit. Alpha wins nothing more. We lose nothing more than we have already lost.
reasoning: The position is structurally losing. Beta cannot exceed level 8, and Alpha has no incentive to drop below 8 since doing so would expose them to Beta gaining oranium (if Alpha drops to 7, Beta at 8 gains 5%; if Alpha drops to 4, Beta gains 20%). Alpha's dominant strategy is to stay at 8 and freeze the 10-0 outcome at the summit. Beta's dominant strategy is also to stay at 8 — any reduction gives Alpha MORE, worsening the outcome. The only scenario where Beta wins is if Alpha believes a de-escalation agreement is credible and genuinely valuable to them. Alpha's 10% is a modest prize given 90% is untouched — there's a slim argument that Alpha should want the pool contested rather than frozen. The diplomatic offer (both to 4) is Beta's only real play: frame it as Alpha leaving 90% on the table. But the game-theoretic reality is Alpha has zero incentive to comply. Maintain 8, minimize further loss, keep diplomatic channel open on the slim chance Alpha miscalculates.
